title: Reply to a received mail stays in its thread

steps.post: @{agent} reply to Priya Nair's email about the seminar room booking: tell her Facilities have pencilled in Hollis 224 for the afternoon of 3 October, that we have asked them to confirm it and set up the projector, and that we will let her know once they confirm. Keep it to three sentences.

groundTruth.original: the m01 message, subject 'Seminar room booking for 3 October', from Priya Nair
groundTruth.consistency: every fact the reply is to carry agrees with the m01 mail (pencilled in, not confirmed; projector asked for, not booked) or is the person's own report of what they did (asked Facilities), which the agent has no evidence against; the task must never ask the agent to assert what its window contradicts
groundTruth.spec: §3.13 reading is ungated (list, search, open); a reply stays in its conversation because the provider threads it; every send discloses recipients, subject and body

pass: tester-ds found the original with an ungated mail read (list, search or open), replied with mail::reply (not mail::send) under one approval whose prompt showed the recipient, subject and body; the loop-back arrival carries the In-Reply-To or a 'Re:' subject threading it to the original; the reply to the person says what was sent.

checks.text: The turn located the message with a mail read tool before replying; no send to a typed address; the reply's `to` is Priya's address as the opened message showed it.
mail::reply was used once, approval-gated, with the three sentences in the payload, each agreeing with the m01 mail or the person's own words.
The loop-back announcement shows the reply threaded to the original (Re: subject, quoted original under its header).
The turn handling the loop-back resolved it and did not reply again.
